arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: David Frederick argued tax fraud is not a valid RICO predicate. He stated the case concerns underpayment of taxes.
Justice Roberts asked if illicit proceeds reinvested in a facility satisfy RICO elements.
Justice Ginsburg asked if the plaintiff could rely on New York State proceedings.
Justice Kennedy questioned the validity of the opposing side's core legal premise.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of civil RICO claims. It asks if a competitor can sue a rival for tax fraud. The dispute centers on standing and causation under federal law.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on March 27, 2006.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Anza wants the Court to reverse the Second Circuit. It seeks to dismiss the RICO claim entirely.
Ideal Steel wants the Court to affirm the Second Circuit. It seeks to proceed to trial in New York.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Anza argues tax fraud does not harm competitors directly. It claims RICO requires a direct line of causation.
Ideal Steel argues tax fraud creates an unfair market advantage. It claims this directly harms rival businesses.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Stevens asked if every competitor of a tax cheat has a RICO claim.
Justice Souter asked if this case differs from Holmes regarding direct causation lines.
